newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: South African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares nudged higher on Wednesday in modest trade as the industrials index pushed forward and offset a slight dip amongst gold shares, dealers said.
"The gold price only perked up quite late. If that had happned earlier it might have changed things," one dealer said.
Dealers said market confidence was still high.
"Underlying sentiment is still very positive, but there is no real aggression behind it" one noted.

A stronger opening from Wall Street, which later turned sour, failed to inspire the market. But dealers said they still widely believed the Dow index would firmly break out above the psychologically important barrier of 6,000 points and inspire a South African rally later in the week.
"Any day now the Dow is going to go through 6,000 and the upward momentum is there that will see us continue better," one dealer said.
Dealers said any such bullish run could soon see the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's all-share index set a new all time high beyond 7,086.8 -- set in April this year.
The all-share index closed at 7,059.1, up 12.2 points, as industrials gained 9.0 points to 8,267.4. Golds eased 3.7 points to 1,742.8.

Most active trade surrounded a handful of blue-chip stocks where a smattering of overseas investors had been spotted trading. De Beers, South African Breweries and Gencor all attracted heavy interest, dealers said.
There was also heavy trade in CNA-Gallo Ltd which saw more than 6.5 million shares traded, but whose share price was unmoved to finish at 385 cents.
De Beers ended flat at 146.25 rand, SA Breweries rose 100 cents to 123 rand and Gencor put on 35 cents to 16.85 rand. Richemont dropped 75 cents to 71.50 rand.

In the futures market worries over weaker bonds saw the industrials contract ease to 8,138/52 from 8,159. The December all-share contract was at 6,600/50 from 6,648 and golds were static at 1,235/41 from 1,238.
